verses.1: And all the people stood up, and they offered their voices. The people wept in that night.
verses.2: And all the children of Israel mourned over Moses and Aaron. They said to them, “All the blessings that were promised to them in Egypt or in this land have been taken away from them.”
verses.3: And why does the LORD bring us to this land, so that our women will be killed and we will be destroyed? It would be better for us to remain in Egypt.
verses.4: And they said to each other, “A head was given back from Egypt.”
verses.5: And Moses and Aaron fell before all the people of Israel.
verses.6: And Joshua ben Nun and Caleb ben Jefneah took possession of the land from the enemies. They divided it among themselves.
verses.7: And they said to all the tribes of Israel, “The land we have crossed through is good. It is indeed a very good land.”
verses.8: If Jehovah desires for us, and brings us to this land, and gives us a land where there is milk and honey.
verses.9: But in Jehovah, do not be afraid. And you shall not fear the people of the earth, for they have shed blood and caused destruction upon themselves. But Jehovah will not let us be afraid.
verses.10: And all the assembly said, “Let us stone them to death. May the glory of Jehovah be seen in the temple of the Lord among all the children of Israel.”
verses.11: And the LORD said to Moses, “Until this people truly believe in me, they will never accept all the things I have done for them.”
verses.12: Let us make you a great nation, and let us exalt you above all other nations.
verses.13: And Moses said to the LORD. And the people of Egypt heard this, because you have brought this people from their land with your power.
verses.14: And they said to the ruler of this land, “Have you heard that You are the LORD among this people? You stand above them in glory. You walk before them by day, and by night, you stand like a cloud. You are like fire at night.”
verses.15: And this people died as one man. And the nations said, “They have heard your name.”
verses.16: I cannot believe that Jehovah could bring this people to the land that was promised them. They were slaughtered in the wilderness.
verses.17: And now, please increase the strength of my Lord, just as you have said.
verses.18: May the LORD prolong our lives and show great kindness. He will not forgive sins or transgressions. He will not punish fathers for their sons’ sins, nor for those who commit evil deeds.
verses.19: Please forgive the sins of this people, for your mercy is great. You brought them out of Egypt and have kept them safe until now.
verses.20: And Jehovah said, “I have forgiven you, as you have said.”
verses.21: But I will live, and the glory of Jehovah will fill all the earth.
verses.22: For all those people who see my glory and the wonders I created in Egypt and in the wilderness, they tried to approach me ten times, but they did not listen to my voice.
verses.23: If they see the land that I have blessed for their ancestors, they will not be able to see it.
verses.24: And my servant became like a cat. Another spirit followed him, and it filled me with joy. It brought him to the land where he was meant to live, and his seed would inherit that land.
verses.25: And the Ammonites and the Canaanites will be confined in the wilderness. Then they will turn around and go towards you, through the Sea of Galilee.
verses.26: And the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
verses.27: Until the day comes when this evil will end. Those who have been tormenting the children of Israel with their punishments will be punished themselves.
verses.28: I say to them, “May the Lord have mercy on you!” If not for what they have spoken in my ears, I would surely do this to them.
verses.29: In this land, their corpses will fall to the ground, and all their possessions will be lost for them. This will happen after they have lived for over forty years.
verses.30: If you come to the land that I have set my hand to prepare for your dwelling in it, then surely, it will be like a little dog that is born and raised by a few people.
verses.31: And those whom you have said would be brought back; I will bring them forth, and they will know the land where you have dwelt.
verses.32: And you will fall in this desert.
verses.33: And among you, there will be those who live in the desert for forty years. They will carry their burdens along with them until they reach the end of the desert.
verses.34: In the forty days that you will spend to possess the land, each day counts as one day of the year. After those forty days have passed, you will know what My covenant is like.
verses.35: I, Jehovah, have said that if I do not do this to all those evil people who are suffering in this region, then they will die there.
verses.36: And the people whom Moses sent to explore the land, they returned and reported all that they had seen about that land.
verses.37: And the people who discovered the treasures of the earth died from the plague before Jehovah.
verses.38: And Joshua ben Nun and Caleb ben Jefneh lived among those people who were going to possess the land.
verses.39: Moses spoke these words to all the children of Israel. The people wept greatly.
verses.40: And they went up in the morning to the top of the mountain, saying, “Let us go up to that place where the Lord said we would go, since we have sinned.”
verses.41: And Moses said, “Why do you cross over the mouth of Jehovah? It will not be successful.”
verses.42: Do not be afraid, for Jehovah is not among you. Do not be terrified before your enemies.
verses.43: For the Ammonites and the Canaanites are there before you. They will fall in battle at Harod. Thus, you will be able to return from your exile, but Jehovah will not be with you.
verses.44: They went up to the top of the mountain. Moses did not leave the camp at all.
verses.45: And the Amalekites and the Canaanites who lived in that mountain descended down. They fought and struggled until they reached Harma.
